user.text:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

history.assistant:
Built the book tracker. The home page shows books you’re reading and books you’ve finished; you can add a book with notes, mark it finished, and open a shareable URL for its detail page. Books persist in data/books.json across restarts. There are no accounts or database.

Run npm start, then open http://localhost:3000. A link shared with someone else requires the server to be reachable from their device.

Verification passed: npm test (2 tests) and npm run build (syntax check), both exit code 0.

tool_steps.assistant: I’ll inspect the project structure and existing stack, then build the book list, add form, detail links, and JSON-file persistence using its conventions.
This is a minimal Node project with no app framework. I’ll use a small server-rendered app so individual book URLs work directly, with writes serialized to a JSON file and no database or accounts.

# Booknotes

A small, no-account bookshelf for books you're reading and books you've finished.

## Run

Requires Node.js 20 or newer. Run `npm start` and visit http://localhost:3000.

Add a book using the form on the home page. Click a book to see its title, author, and notes, or mark it finished. Every book has its own URL (`/books/<id>`), which you can copy and share with someone who can access this server. To make links available outside your computer, host the app on a reachable server; `localhost` links only work on your machine.

Books are saved to `data/books.json` beside the app, and remain after restarting it. This directory is ignored by Git. Set `BOOKS_FILE` to an alternate JSON file path or `PORT` to change the listening port. Back up the JSON file to keep your books. The app is intended for a trusted environment; it has no accounts or access control.

Run checks with `npm test` and `npm run build`.
